# Unreleased

Staging note for the next release. Fold it into that release's `<tag>.md` (the release job reads `.github/release-notes/<tag>.md`) and delete this file.

## New

- **Drag files, folders, images and text into the chat input.** A workspace file dropped from the VS Code Explorer or an editor tab becomes an `@` file chip (read when you send, as if picked from the `@` list); a folder becomes an `@` folder chip, which is a search scope rather than the folder's whole contents. Images go through the image attachment (only for models that read images; at most 10 per message, 5 MB each), dropped text loses hidden characters, and a link is added as text without being fetched. Files that look like they hold secrets (`.env` files, keys and certificates, `.ssh` and cloud credential folders), files outside the workspace, and files from the operating system's file manager other than images are refused, and the input says which file and why; a refused file is never read. In VS Code, hold Shift while dragging. VS Code 1.140 and later stop Explorer and tab drops from reaching extension webviews (microsoft/vscode#339036); until VS Code fixes that, use `@` for workspace files. JetBrains IDEs are reported not to deliver drops to the chat (its browser is off-screen); use `@` there.
- **Bedrock: a 0 quota is named before the first request.** If your AWS credentials may read Service Quotas (`servicequotas:ListServiceQuotas`, optional), Test connection and selecting a Bedrock model warn when the account's tokens-per-minute (or requests-per-minute) quota for that model is 0 in the region, with a link to the Service Quotas console: "<model> has a 0 tokens-per-minute quota in <region> for this account; request an increase in Service Quotas". Without the permission, Test connection still succeeds and shows one quiet line, "Quota check skipped: this profile lacks servicequotas:ListServiceQuotas"; that answer is remembered per profile and region for a day (or until the credentials change). Throttling, network errors, a region without Service Quotas and slow answers (5 seconds) are skipped quietly; nothing waits for the check. A Bedrock API key cannot read Service Quotas, so the check is skipped for it.
- **Bedrock prices from the AWS Price List.** Cost estimates for Bedrock models use the AWS Price List for the selected model's region, ahead of the built-in prices, and name it with its date. Flex and priority requests are priced at their own rates where AWS lists them. The file is public (no credentials, no IAM) and is downloaded from `pricing.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` only when a Bedrock model is configured, under **Model information updates** (Automatic: on selecting a Bedrock model and once per refresh interval; Only when I ask: on Bedrock Test connection; Off: never). Firewall allowlists: expect `pricing.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` and `servicequotas.<region>.amazonaws.com` (TCP 443) on machines with a Bedrock model.

## Behaviour changes

- **OpenRouter's model list is now refreshed automatically, by default. This reverses the 2.16.0 privacy promise** that `openrouter.ai` is contacted only when you choose Pull now or Refresh. With the new setting **Model information updates** on **Automatic** (the default), Continuous downloads OpenRouter's public model list (names, context sizes, per-token prices for cost estimates and `--max-budget-usd`, tool support) in the background whenever the copy on this computer is missing or older than 24 hours: about 15 to 60 seconds after the IDE starts, 1 to 3 seconds after the terminal agent starts, and again once a day while it runs. This happens even if you do not use OpenRouter. The request is one GET to `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models` with no key, account, prompt or body, and only `accept` and `user-agent: continuous` headers; nothing waits for it, failures are retried with backoff (5 minutes up to 6 hours) and the list you had stays in use. Provider setup no longer asks "Pull the latest model information from OpenRouter?" in Automatic mode; the model step, the Models settings page and the console's Total Usage show "OpenRouter model information last updated <time> · Refresh now".
  - **To turn it off**: set `continuous.modelInformationUpdates` to `off` in VS Code (or choose Off on the Models settings page), or add `modelCatalog: off` to `~/.continuous/config.yaml` (read by JetBrains and the terminal agent too), or set `CONTINUOUS_MODEL_INFO_UPDATES=off`. Off never contacts `openrouter.ai` and uses the bundled model data. **Only when I ask** (`modelCatalog: manual`) keeps the 2.16.0 behaviour. If you chose "Don't ask again" in 2.16.0 or 2.16.1 (`modelCatalog: never`), nothing changes for you: no background refresh and no question. The interval is `continuous.modelInformationRefreshHours` / `modelCatalogRefreshHours` (default 24).
  - `continuous models refresh` is refused when updates are off.
  - **Ollama is unchanged**: `ollama.com` is still contacted only when you choose Download or Refresh in Ollama's setup, never at start-up or on a timer, and the new setting does not apply to it.
  - Firewall and sandbox allowlists: expect `openrouter.ai` (TCP 443) shortly after start-up on a machine whose list is missing or stale.

## Fixes

- Bedrock errors now name the cause when a model is refused for quota or account reasons. "Not available for this account" (what Bedrock answers when the account's tokens-per-minute quota for the model is 0, even with model access granted) points at Service Quotas instead of the model access page; "your account is currently being verified" (the first use of a region) says to wait; a throttled request says the quota is used up and that throttling on the very first request can mean a quota of 0.
- Costs now carry where their prices came from and as of when (Anthropic list prices, OpenAI pricing page, AWS Price List, the downloaded OpenRouter list, or a price you entered), for the cost displays to show. When Bedrock or Anthropic report that a request was served at a non-standard tier (flex, priority, batch), the cost breakdown says the figure is the standard-tier price and whether the actual charge is lower or higher.
- Adding Anthropic models reads image support and the scheduled retirement date from Anthropic's model list, and the Bedrock model list keeps image support and the legacy, extended-access and end-of-life dates Bedrock reports.
- Bedrock no longer fails with "no content in assistant message before conversational turn change". A turn that converts to nothing (a reply stopped or failed before any text, reasoning a non-Claude model can't take back, a tool call without an id, a user message whose context or image rendered empty) is now left out and the turns around it are joined, so the request keeps the alternating roles Converse requires. The CLI, which sent two messages of the same role in that case, gets the same repair. A history that was already valid is sent byte for byte as before, so prompt caching is unaffected.
